wwv.schedule_notes: Per NIST (format page updated 2024-09-03): seconds ticks are 5 ms of 1000 Hz, omitted at seconds 29 and 59; minute marker 800 ms of 1000 Hz; hour marker 800 ms of 1500 Hz. Each tick sits in a 40 ms protected zone (10 ms silence, 5 ms tone, 25 ms silence). Audio tones: 500 Hz and 600 Hz alternate per the minute lists; 440 Hz in minute 2 (omitted during the first hour of each UTC day); no tone in minutes 0, 8-10, 18, 29-30, 43-51, 59. Voice time announcement every minute, ~7.5 s before the minute (WWVH's comes first at ~15 s before). Geophysical alert (NOAA, < 45 s) at minute 18, updated every 3 h (typically 0000, 0300 ... 2100 UTC). HamSCI/NIST ionospheric test signal (tones, chirps, noise bursts) at minute 8 since 2021-11-15. UT1 correction: doubled ticks in seconds 1-8 (+) or 9-16 (-), 0.1 s each. BCD time code on a 100 Hz subcarrier, 1 bit/s. Modulation: double-sideband AM; 50% tones, 50% time code, 100% ticks/markers, 75% voice. Station ID at minutes 0 and 30 is from NIST SP 432 (2002) Figure 3.7. Marine storm warnings (minutes 8-11 in SP 432) were discontinued 2019-01-31 1800 UTC (NWS SCN 18-102). GPS status announcements at minutes 14-15 (SP 432, 2002) are not on the current NIST page and their status is unverified; the current tone table puts tones in those minutes. Recent outage on record: 2026-10-19 2011-2034 UTC on all frequencies (NIST outages page).

wwv.power_note: 10 kW on 10 and 15 MHz, 5 kW on 2.5 MHz; 5 MHz normally 10 kW but NIST says it currently runs 5 kW due to equipment failure (page updated 2026-06-22).
wwv.voice_time_utc: Female voice, about 15 s before each minute.
wwv.schedule_notes: Ticks are 5 ms of 1200 Hz (omitted at seconds 29 and 59); minute marker 800 ms of 1200 Hz; hour marker 800 ms of 1500 Hz. 440 Hz in minute 1 (omitted in the first UTC hour of the day). No tone in minutes 0, 8-10, 14-19, 29-30. Geophysical alert at minute 45. HamSCI test signal at minute 48 since 2021-11-15. Station ID at minutes 29 and 59 is from NIST SP 432 (2002) Figure 3.8. Marine storm warnings (minutes 48-52 in SP 432) discontinued 2019-01-31 (NWS SCN 18-102). GPS status at minutes 43-44 (SP 432) unverified/likely gone; the current tone table lists 500 Hz tones in those minutes. Note the tone lists overlap in minute 48 (500 Hz listed) and the HamSCI signal; NIST says the test signal 'may be modified occasionally'.

stanag_pactor_notes: PACTOR/Winlink (amateur): in the US, an automatically controlled digital station (which is what an unattended Winlink RMS is) may transmit RTTY or data only in these HF segments: 3.585-3.600, 7.100-7.105, 10.140-10.150, 14.0950-14.0995, 14.1005-14.112, 18.105-18.110, 21.090-21.100, 24.925-24.930, 28.120-28.189 MHz (plus 6 m and up), or elsewhere when responding to a locally/remotely controlled station with a signal no wider than 500 Hz (47 CFR 97.221, eCFR fetched 2026-11-06: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-97/subpart-C/section-97.221). Winlink publishes its live RMS channel list at https://winlink.org/RMSChannels (it changes; not copied here; the page sits behind a bot challenge so it was not read). STANAG 4285 (NATO HF single-tone PSK modem per the wiki: 2400 Bd, 75-3600 bps, BPSK/QPSK/8PSK, short/long interleave, ~2.75 kHz bandwidth, USB): the Signal Identification Wiki says it is 'found on many HF frequencies between 1.89 MHz to 22.7 MHz' and points to the Utility DXers Forum logs for current usage (https://www.sigidwiki.com/wiki/STANAG_4285, a community reference, not an official one). No specific STANAG 4285 stations are listed because none could be verified from an official source.
